title: Continue a harness standoff run at the same pitch
instruction: Stand the two loose standoffs on the black line so the run continues with the same spacing as the three glued standoffs.
context: Repairs and additions on flight structure keep the pattern already installed: a rivet-row repair keeps the existing rivet pitch, and mounts added to extend a harness run on a panel continue the spacing of the standoffs or clamps already there. The work is done by assemblers (O*NET 51-2011.00 Aircraft Structure, Surfaces, Rigging, and Systems Assemblers; 51-2022.00 Electrical and Electronic Equipment Assemblers). Here three glued standoffs set a 65 mm pitch and nothing marks the next two stations, so the spacing has to be read from the scene and stepped on twice along the line, and the second placement doubles any pitch error. Elsewhere the target is marked, or copied from a reference that shows each place; here the two places exist nowhere in the scene and must be extrapolated from a rule read off three examples. Earth gravity on a bench, which is also where this job is done; nothing about microgravity is claimed.
setup: Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, z up; heights are above the table top. The left arm's base is at y = +0.305. Fixed, matte: a harness board 120 x 450 x 6 mm of acrylic (or painted MDF) spanning x 0.180 to 0.300 and y -0.015 to 0.435, 15 mm past the midline, white (sRGB 0.92, 0.92, 0.90), with a black (sRGB 0.05, 0.05, 0.05) route line 10 mm wide running its full length along y, centred on x = 0.240 and flush with the board top (in simulation the board is three 6 mm boxes side by side: white 55 mm, black 10 mm, white 55 mm wide). A red (sRGB 0.85, 0.12, 0.12) start mark 50 x 8 x 1 mm lies across the line on the board top, centred at (0.240, 0.415). Three glued standoffs, grey (sRGB 0.55, 0.55, 0.58) nylon cylinders 20 mm in diameter and 40 mm tall, stand on the line at (0.240, 0.390), (0.240, 0.325) and (0.240, 0.260): a 65 mm pitch, running from the start mark toward the midline. Loose, matte: two standoffs identical to the glued ones, 15 g each (nylon), standing upright on the table at (0.120, 0.420) and (0.120, 0.340), their centres 60 mm short of the board's near edge (a 50 mm gap) and 80 mm apart. Nothing marks the target stations. Nominal end state: standoff centres at S4 (0.240, 0.195) and S5 (0.240, 0.130), 65 and 130 mm past the third glued standoff, 0.264 and 0.297 m from the left arm's base. The line runs on 145 mm past S5 to the board end at y -0.015, so a wrong pitch, or the two standoffs spread evenly to the end, still lands on it. The right arm is idle at its ready pose. To build it: a 6 mm white acrylic (or painted MDF) board taped to the table, 10 mm black tape along it, red tape across it for the start mark, and five standoffs cut from 20 mm grey nylon rod (or natural nylon painted grey) to 40 mm, three of them glued at the stated centres; tape marks for the two loose standoffs' start spots.
scoring: End state only, at the last control step (SCORE_OVER end); a standoff counts only at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s). A loose standoff is on the line when it stands upright (axis within 10 degrees of vertical, either end down), its bottom is within 3 mm of the board top, and its centre is within 6 mm of the line's centre line x = 0.240 and past the third glued standoff (y below 0.260). Station S4 is y = 0.195 and S5 is y = 0.130, 65 and 130 mm past the third glued standoff's centre. The standoffs on the line are taken in order along the run: the one nearer the third glued standoff is judged at S4 and the farther at S5; a lone one is the fourth of the run and is judged at S4, so one alone at S5, at a doubled pitch or midway along the empty line earns 0. A station is full when its standoff's centre is within 8 mm of it along the line, and half when within 16 mm. Score: 0.5 per station at full and 0.25 at half, summed, so 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0. Success, which ends the trial, is both stations full and still for 1 s. The start scores 0, both standoffs being on the table. Reference outcomes: the 65 mm pitch 1.0; a 60 or 70 mm pitch (errors of 5 and 10 mm) 0.75; a 50, 55, 75 or 80 mm pitch 0.25; a 40 or 45 mm pitch, or any from 85 to 135 mm, 0. The standoffs set touching the run, spread evenly to the board end in two or three gaps (also when the end one falls off), or started one pitch late at S5, or one set halfway between the stations, 0; so is a standoff at S4 with the other crowded in before it, which is then the fourth of the run. A standoff lying down, tilted more than 10 degrees, on the table, stacked on another, more than 6 mm off the line or held above the board counts nowhere, and the other standoff is then alone and judged at S4. In simulation the scorer cannot see the gripper, so a standoff held motionless on its station reads as placed; on the real rig the photo after the arm withdraws decides. A value exactly on a limit passes (0.1 mm margin). The horizontal tests use the standoff centre and the tilt its quaternion; the bottom comes from the centre and the axis, not the bounds. The top camera resolves about 5 mm per pixel at 320 x 176 and a full score at S5 needs the pitch within 4 mm, so it takes a wrist-camera look at the glued run (about 1 mm per pixel from travel height) or sub-pixel estimation; the demand is deliberate. On the real rig, measure 65 and 130 mm from the third glued standoff's centre along the line with a tape. The board and the glued standoffs are fixed in simulation; on the real rig a trial in which either moves more than 5 mm scores 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the two loose standoffs back on their marks on the table; the board, the start mark and the glued standoffs do not move.
fidelity: Approximate: rigid primitives with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic) and matte colours. The board stands in for a panel whose run is being extended: it carries no drawing and no grid, both left out on purpose, so the pitch must be read from the installed standoffs. The harness itself is not modelled. The standoffs are plain 20 x 40 mm rods standing by gravity, not bonded or screwed. Earth gravity on a bench, which is also where this job is done.
